title: Protesters in Paris demonstrate against living costs and police powers bill
seoTitle: Paris protest against living costs and police

tea.why: Protesters oppose rising living costs, public service cuts, and a proposed law granting police greater protection when using weapons.
tea.want: They demand better living conditions, the withdrawal of the police powers bill, and higher wages.
tea.changed: Nov 14: Protests occurred across France, with 219 people arrested following clashes between demonstrators and police.

summary: On November 14, 2026, demonstrators gathered in Paris and other French cities for the fifth consecutive Saturday to protest against the rising cost of living and a proposed police powers bill. The legislation, which would presume police acted in self-defense when using weapons, has been criticized by activists as a potential license for police brutality. Participants included students, union members, and Yellow Vest activists. While the interior minister estimated 106,000 participants nationwide with 24,000 in Paris, student unions claimed the total reached 200,000. Clashes were reported in several cities, leading to 219 arrests. Authorities deployed tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds. In response to ongoing unrest, the government announced a 1.6% minimum wage increase, though unions have rejected this as insufficient and called for a national strike.
demands: Withdrawal of the police powers bill
response: The government announced a 1.6% minimum wage increase starting in December and initiated month-long negotiations with unions regarding low wages. The interior minister reported the turnout figures.

crowd.text: Student unions estimated 200,000 participants nationwide, while the interior minister stated 106,000.

updates.text: Protests held across France against living costs and a police powers bill; 219 arrests reported.
